speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a child presenting with a limp and localized pain but no fever, I need to start by asking: Does the pain occur in a specific spot on your leg, and can you point to it for me?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; it is clear he is favoring his left leg due to left knee pain. In a 7-year-old with no trauma or fever, could you describe the exact location of the pain—does it hurt only at the knee, or does it extend up the thigh or down toward the ankle?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (or Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis), though the knee pain may be referred pain from the hip. I recommend requesting an X-Ray of the left hip and knee to confirm. REQUEST IMAGES: Left Hip and Knee X-Ray
